rows.evidence: Q1: Methods Sections 2.1-2.2 and Results Sections 3.1-3.3 report the authors' own comparison of OpenET-based irrigation calculations with farmer records (239 field-years) and WIMAS flowmeter data in the SD-6 LEMA at field, water right group and management area scales (Tables 1-3, Figs. 3-8).
rows.notes: The study does not report any result of its own on remote sensing delivering water savings. It evaluates how accurately ET-based water balance calculations reproduce reported irrigation withdrawals/applications. The 20% allocation, the 26-31% pumping reduction and the slowed water-table decline in the SD-6 LEMA are cited from other work (Drysdale and Hendricks 2018; Deines et al. 2019; Butler et al. 2020; Whittemore et al. 2023) in Section 2.1.2, not measured here. Moreover, the study does not claim that remotely sensed ET was used to enforce the LEMA; the enforcement relies on flowmeters, and the paper explicitly concludes that variability across ET models exceeds the signal of the conservation measures (Section 4.1.3, Conclusions). At most the study supports a precondition: that remote sensing can approximately estimate irrigation water use, which could in future support data-driven regulation.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methods Sections 2.1-2.2 and Results Sections 3.1-3.3 report the authors' own comparison of OpenET-based irrigation calculations with farmer irrigation records and statewide flowmeter data at three spatial scales (Tables 1-3, Figs. 3-8).
rows.notes: The study reports no data on crop yield or productivity. The statement that the LEMA's pumping reduction had only minor negative impacts on yield and none on profitability is cited from Golden (2018) in Section 2.1.2, not an own result. The study's own results concern the accuracy and uncertainty of ET-based irrigation estimates (bias, MAE, R2) relative to reported irrigation; nothing links remote sensing to yield outcomes. Upstream not set because the study does not even address a precondition of the yield effect.

notes: Full text appears complete. The review appears to have attributed to this paper findings about the SD-6 LEMA (20% pumping reduction, water savings, minimal yield losses) that the paper only cites as background from earlier studies; the paper's own contribution is an accuracy/uncertainty assessment of ET-derived irrigation estimates against metered data.
